body_text:
Let $N \trianglelefteq G$ be a normal subgroup. The set of left
cosets $G/N = \{gN : g \in G\}$ forms a group under the operation
$(gN)(hN) = (gh)N$, called the *quotient group* (or factor group)
of $G$ by $N$.

*Proof of Well-Definedness*: Suppose $g_1N = g_2N$ and
$h_1N = h_2N$. Then $g_2 = g_1 n_1$ and $h_2 = h_1 n_2$ for some
$n_1, n_2 \in N$. Then:
$$ g_2 h_2 = (g_1 n_1)(h_1 n_2) = g_1 (n_1 h_1) n_2. $$ Since $N$
is normal, $n_1 h_1 = h_1 n_3$ for some $n_3 \in N$. Substituting
gives $g_2 h_2 = g_1 (h_1 n_3) n_2 = (g_1 h_1)(n_3 n_2)$. Since
$n_3 n_2 \in N$, we have $(g_2 h_2)N = (g_1 h_1)N$. Thus
multiplication is independent of the chosen representatives.

The identity of $G/N$ is $eN = N$, and the inverse of $gN$ is
$g^{-1}N$. If $N$ is not normal, coset multiplication depends on
representative choices and fails to define an operation on $G/N$.
